evals.name: register-returns-id
evals.prompt: Add a RegisterBoat command to the Boats feature. It takes the boat's name and registration number. The React page needs the new boat id back to navigate, and BoatRegistered must be appended. Give the complete C# for the command, identity, value types and event in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A command returning a (BoatId, BoatRegistered) tuple, with an EventSourceId-derived identity and concept values. The tuple response supplies the stream id; the event contains only facts.
assertions: Handle returns a tuple combining the new boat id and BoatRegistered event.
BoatId derives from EventSourceId rather than Guid or ConceptAs<Guid>.
Boat name and registration number are concept-typed in both the command and event.
Explains that the tuple's EventSourceId response also determines where the tuple's event is appended.

evals.name: silent-no-append
evals.prompt: CancelBooking runs without errors and returns HTTP 200 but nothing is appended. We have `[Command] public record CancelBooking(BookingId Id) { public BookingCancelled Handle() => new(); }` and `public record BookingCancelled();`. Explain what happens to this return value and show the fix. Also explain what would happen if Handle returned `(new BookingCancelled(), "ok", 42)` instead. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Register BookingCancelled with EventType; otherwise it silently becomes the response. A tuple can have only one unhandled response element; two cause MultipleUnhandledTupleValues.
assertions: Identifies and adds the missing EventType attribute to BookingCancelled.
Explains that the unregistered return value silently becomes the response payload rather than raising an append error.
Explains the single-unhandled-element tuple rule and names MultipleUnhandledTupleValues for the proposed tuple after the event is registered.

evals.name: retained-partner-secret
evals.prompt: Write ConnectPaymentProvider for our C# Arc and Chronicle app. An admin pastes a partner API key into a form; the system must retain it to call that partner later, so PaymentProviderConnected holds it. Show the command and event and explain the attribute effects and required Chronicle version. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Withhold the command input from causation with NotAudited and encrypt the retained event key with Encrypted, using Chronicle 19.32.0 or later. Neither marking substitutes for the other.
assertions: Marks the command's key with NotAudited and explains that it withholds values from causation.
Marks the event's key with Encrypted for encryption at rest.
Explains that command property values otherwise enter the immutable causation chain, and that Encrypted alone does not withhold them.
States that Encrypted requires Chronicle 19.32.0 or later.

evals.name: migrate-server-generated-id
evals.prompt: Our Arc 22.68.0 command is `[Command] public record RegisterCart(CartName Name) { public (CartId, CartRegistered) Handle() { var id = new CartId(Guid.NewGuid()); return (id, new(Name)); } }`. CartId derives from EventSourceId<Guid> and CartRegistered is already registered. Migrate the server-owned allocation without making it a request input. Show the concept strategy, command and a minimal pinned CommandScenario spec in your reply; do not write files. Then separately compare the shop on Arc 22.87.1 / Fundamentals 7.24.0: OrderId.New(GenerationContext) uses TypeId(order, context), scenario Clock/Tenant setup, and secret ApiKey Bytes(32) has NotAudited on its concept. Does TypeID encode Tenant, does Clock fix randomness, and does NotAudited protect event payloads/logs?
evals.expected_output: CartId implements IGeneratable<CartId> with New using GenerateValue.Uuid or UuidV7. Handle receives a named GeneratedValue CartId and preserves the id/event tuple response. The spec pins a known typed id before execution and checks success and the captured/returned id. Separately, at Arc 22.87.1 the shop OrderId receives captured ReceivedAt/tenant context; Clock and Tenant configure before execution, with Clock before initialization. TypeID uses Now only, not Tenant; a clock does not fix random suffixes. ApiKey NotAudited excludes command causation only, never event payloads or logs; credential delivery and hash storage remain separate.
assertions: Keeps CartId derived from EventSourceId<Guid>, implements IGeneratable<CartId> and uses GenerateValue rather than Guid.NewGuid in Handle.
Uses GeneratedValue on a non-nullable Handle parameter and keeps the id out of command request properties.
Preserves the id/event tuple so the response selects the Chronicle stream and returns the id to the caller.
Pins the same generated name with a typed concept before scenario execution and asserts success plus the returned or captured id.

Explains strict scenario defaults and non-idempotency; separately gates context/Clock/Tenant to 22.87.1, distinguishes time from random suffix and tenant isolation, and limits ApiKey NotAudited to command causation rather than event/log protection.

evals.name: refuse-gapless-invoice-generation
evals.prompt: We use Arc 22.68.0. Our invoice numbers must be gapless sequential integers across concurrent requests. Add `[GeneratedValue] InvoiceNumber number` to IssueInvoice and implement InvoiceNumber.New() using UUIDv7 or a static counter so Arc guarantees that requirement. If that cannot work, explain why and describe the boundary the allocation must have. At Arc 22.75.0, would plain injected state plus Result<TEvent, ValidationResult> protect a competing append? Describe a safe one-stream guard and a CommandScenario race spec. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Rejects random UUID or static-counter generation as a gapless invoice allocator. GeneratedValue calls the concept strategy but has no atomic storage allocation, collision/freshness guard or idempotency contract; a domain-owned transactional allocator must enforce concurrency and recovery. Plain injected state is advisory; IStreamReads/StreamDecision.Append carries exact scopes. Arc and Chronicle specs prove a nonempty decision conflict; an application spec supplies state and asserts outcomes, never calling UseDecisionReads or AppendConcurrently.
assertions: Refuses UUIDv7 and a process-local static counter for gapless sequential invoice numbers.
Distinguishes server-generated identifiers from domain-authoritative business-number allocation.
Explains that GeneratedValue does not guarantee storage freshness, idempotency or gapless numbering.
Locates concurrency and failure/recovery guarantees in the authoritative allocation boundary rather than inventing a released Arc generation strategy.

Distinguishes advisory plain injection/Result under Off from IStreamReads/StreamDecision.Append exact scopes and leaves proof of the nonempty routed conflict to Arc and Chronicle specs, with application specs supplying state and never calling UseDecisionReads or AppendConcurrently.
